first_impression.reaction: Okay, the first paragraph actually tells me what a garden wedding is and the one catch (weather), so I didn't bounce. But then Key Takeaways mostly tells me what's further down the page instead of just giving me the tips. On a phone on the train I want the answers in that box, not a table of contents.

journey.quote: It works when the styling and the backup plan are decided together, because the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather.
journey.reaction: Good. Straight answer and a real point in the first two sentences. That's why I kept going.

journey.quote: The styling ideas cover the aisle, long tables, florals and greenery, dusk lighting, lounges and stationery.
journey.reaction: This is a list of topics, not a takeaway. I'd rather this said the actual idea so I don't have to scroll for it.

journey.quote: The eight real garden weddings below come from our own published stories, each linked to the full account.
journey.reaction: Fine, but this tells me about your website, not about my wedding. Wasted bullet for me.

journey.section: Real garden weddings from our pages
journey.quote: Eight couples and eight gardens, each described as their own story tells it.
journey.reaction: Then eight headings that are just names of people I don't know. When I'm scrolling I can't tell which one is the courtyard one or the marquee one without reading every paragraph.

journey.quote: Put the front rows, and the grandparents, where the shade falls at the hour of the ceremony, with every row on level ground.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of tip I'd screenshot. Practical and I wouldn't have thought of it.

journey.quote: Design the lighting for the hour your reception ends, not the hour it begins.
journey.reaction: Nice, short and useful. Easy to skim.

journey.section: Wet weather plan and covered space
journey.quote: Where is the covered space, and does it hold every guest seated for both the ceremony and dinner?
journey.reaction: The question lists are the most useful part of the page. I'd bookmark it for these when I start talking to venues.

journey.quote: Australian sun safety advice recommends sun protection whenever the UV level reaches 3 or higher, and UV cannot be seen or felt, so check the UV forecast for the location on the SunSmart app or the Bureau of Meteorology website.
journey.reaction: Linked to an actual health source, which I trust. Very Australia-specific though, and I'm not necessarily in Australia.

journey.quote: The wedding moves to the covered space agreed with the venue. Before you book, confirm where it is, that it holds every guest seated, and who makes the call and by what time.
journey.reaction: Short FAQ answers that actually answer. Good.

journey.section: Plan your garden wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: I don't know who you are and I came for ideas, so I'm not filling in a form. Doesn't annoy me though, it's at the bottom where it belongs and there were no pop-ups.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much more (or less) does a garden wedding cost than an indoor one? The page never touches cost at all.
Is this up to date? There's no date or 'updated' line anywhere, so I can't tell if it's still true in 2026.
What's the best time of year for a garden wedding? It tells me to ask the venue, but gives me no general steer.
Does any of the sun and weather advice apply if I'm not getting married in Australia?

turn_offs_found.quote: Every planning point is a question for the venue, starting with the wet weather plan and where the covered space sits.
turn_offs_found.why: Key Takeaways describes the article instead of giving me the answer. The real answer (confirm covered space for every guest seated, who calls it and by when) is further down.
Headings that are couples' names don't match anything I searched for, so the section is hard to skim on a phone.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the venue question lists
A friend who's looking at an outdoor venue

cta_reaction.quote: Tell Wedded Concierge the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming.
cta_reaction.why: I only just found this site from Google and I'm still at the ideas stage. I might bookmark the page, but I'm not enquiring with a planner yet.

top_3_changes: Key takeaways, bullet 2. Old: "The styling ideas cover the aisle, long tables, florals and greenery, dusk lighting, lounges and stationery." New: "Let the garden do the styling: use an existing path for the aisle, keep aisle markers and centrepieces low, and design the lighting for the hour your reception ends."

Key takeaways, bullet 3. Old: "Every planning point is a question for the venue, starting with the wet weather plan and where the covered space sits." New: "Before you book, confirm the covered space holds every guest seated for the ceremony and dinner, who makes the call to move under cover, and by what time."

Real garden weddings intro. Old: "Eight couples and eight gardens, each described as their own story tells it." New: "Eight couples and eight gardens, from a courtyard and a flower ceiling to marquees on the lawn and a family estate. Tap a name for the full story."

At most 3 suggested edits with exact old/new strings

assumptions: The query 'garden wedding' is read as mostly ideas/inspiration intent, with some planning intent.
Read on a phone: the in-brief section, Key Takeaways, a skim of the real weddings, one styling section, the venue questions and the FAQ, as the persona's decision behaviour allows.

open_questions.question: Should the post carry a visible 'updated' date? This persona looks for dated information and the draft shows none.
Cost is the persona's first instinct and the page never mentions it. Is a cost pointer (e.g. a link to an existing budget article, if one exists) in scope, given price claims need sign-off?
